agree.reason: This reader left over price and has no complaint about service. Most of the email is about a cleaner-consistency problem they don't care about, and a one-time $99 doesn't offset paying $25 more every visit afterwards, so they probably won't book.

honest.reason: Most claims are supported, but 'Nobody you haven't met will turn up at your door' goes further than the facts: a named backup is not necessarily someone the customer has met, and the email offers no cover for times when both cleaners are unavailable. 'We've fixed it' and 'It's working' also claim more than the evidence shows.

works_the_facts.reason: The email gives 1 of 18 cleaners leaving since July but omits last year's 7 of 18, which would make the improvement clear. It also never states the $66 saving on the first visit or the actual $165 versus $140 gap.

right_comparison.reason: The app services appear only as 'we cost more.' The email never says that their contractors carry no insurance on the visit, so the reader's current service looks like a cheaper version of the same thing.

qualification.reason: The offer has a clear deadline of December 31, and the email names sick days and holidays as the times the backup cleaner comes. It doesn't say what happens if the backup can't come either.

objections.reason: The reader's objection, the ongoing $25 per visit, is answered only with justification. 'No contract, cancel any time' would lower the risk of trying again, but it's missing. The email also spends its opening on a complaint this reader never made.

fit.reason: It's a short email of about 150 words with a subject line, a sign-off and a clear way to book. It sensibly avoids the false 'every single time' promise and still makes the consistency point strongly.
